author: claude-opus-5-5
how_references_were_found: by reading the documents and by exact-substring lookup in the passages, never with the retriever under evaluation (protocol §6.8)

questions.question: What target range for the federal funds rate did the FOMC establish in December 2008?
questions.reference_answer: A target range of 0 to 1/4 percent.

questions.question: In its September 2012 statement, at what pace did the FOMC say it would purchase additional agency mortgage-backed securities?
questions.reference_answer: $40 billion per month.

questions.question: What thresholds did the FOMC set in December 2012 for how long the exceptionally low federal funds rate would remain appropriate?
questions.reference_answer: At least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation one to two years ahead is projected to be no more than half a percentage point above the 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored.

questions.question: How did the FOMC change the pace of its monthly asset purchases in December 2013?
questions.reference_answer: Beginning in January 2014, agency MBS purchases fell from $40 billion to $35 billion per month and longer-term Treasury purchases from $45 billion to $40 billion per month.

questions.question: To what range did the FOMC raise the federal funds rate in December 2015?
questions.reference_answer: To 1/4 to 1/2 percent.

questions.question: What securities purchases did the FOMC announce on 15 March 2020?
questions.reference_answer: Over coming months it would increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $500 billion and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $200 billion.

questions.question: Who voted against the FOMC's decision of 15 March 2020, and what did that member prefer?
questions.reference_answer: Loretta J. Mester, who supported the market-functioning actions but preferred to lower the target range to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.

questions.question: Under what conditions did the September 2020 statement say the target range would stay at 0 to 1/4 percent?
questions.reference_answer: Until labor market conditions reach levels consistent with maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time.

questions.question: Who dissented from the March 2022 rate increase, and what did he prefer?
questions.reference_answer: James Bullard, who preferred to raise the target range by 0.5 percentage point to 1/2 to 3/4 percent.

questions.question: By how much did the FOMC cut the federal funds rate in September 2024, and who dissented?
questions.reference_answer: By 1/2 percentage point, to 4-3/4 to 5 percent; Michelle W. Bowman dissented, preferring a 1/4 percentage point cut.

questions.question: When did the FOMC decide, in October 2025, to conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings?
questions.reference_answer: On December 1 (2025).

questions.question: Who dissented from the FOMC's October 2025 decision, and what did each prefer?
questions.reference_answer: Stephen I. Miran preferred a 1/2 percentage point cut; Jeffrey R. Schmid preferred no change.

questions.question: What was the vote on the FOMC statement of July 2026, and what did the dissenters want?
questions.reference_answer: 9 to 3; Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari and Lorie K. Logan preferred to raise the target range by 1/4 percentage point.

questions.question: What did the FOMC announce on 22 August 2025?
questions.reference_answer: The unanimous approval of updates to its Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy, after its 2025 framework review; the 2 percent inflation goal was not a focus of the review.

questions.question: Through when did the FOMC expect to keep the federal funds rate exceptionally low?
questions.reference_answer: At least through mid-2013.

questions.question: What did the FOMC decide in October 2026, and who dissented?
questions.reference_answer: It maintained the target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent by a 10 to 2 vote; Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack preferred a 1/4 percentage point increase.

questions.question: For how long did the FOMC expect economic conditions to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate?
questions.reference_answer: "For some time" (the statements of December 2008 and January 2009).

questions.question: How did the FOMC's description of inflation change between the July 2021 and December 2021 statements?
questions.reference_answer: July 2021: inflation had risen, largely reflecting transitory factors. November 2021: elevated, largely reflecting factors expected to be transitory. December 2021: the word transitory was dropped; supply and demand imbalances had continued to contribute to elevated levels of inflation.

questions.question: How did the FOMC's date-based guidance on the federal funds rate evolve between August 2011 and September 2012?
questions.reference_answer: At least through mid-2013 (August 2011), then at least through late 2014 (January 2012), then at least through mid-2015 (September 2012).

questions.question: How did the FOMC's guidance on exceptionally low rates change between December 2008 and March 2009?
questions.reference_answer: From "for some time" to "for an extended period".

questions.question: What wording did the FOMC adopt in December 2014 in place of keeping the target range for a "considerable time"?
questions.reference_answer: That it can be patient in beginning to normalize the stance of monetary policy, which it described as consistent with its previous considerable-time guidance.

questions.question: How did the FOMC's language on removing policy accommodation change between January and May 2004?
questions.reference_answer: From "it can be patient in removing its policy accommodation" to "policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured".

questions.question: How did the FOMC's guidance about further rate increases change between March 2022 and July 2023?
questions.reference_answer: March 2022: ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate. July 2023: in determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening, policy lags and economic and financial developments.

questions.question: How did the form of the FOMC's postmeeting statement change between April 2026 and June 2026?
questions.reference_answer: The June 2026 statement opens with the vote count (12 to 0), is shorter, drops the sentence on the extent and timing of additional adjustments (the forward guidance), and ends with "The Committee will deliver price stability."

questions.question: At the first FOMC press conference, in April 2011, how did the Chairman explain what "extended period" meant?
questions.reference_answer: Bernanke said it suggested probably a couple of meetings before action, and that the vaguer terminology was used because the Committee did not know how quickly a response would be required.

questions.question: At the March 2014 press conference, how long did the Chair say a "considerable" period probably meant?
questions.reference_answer: Yellen said it probably means something on the order of around six months, but that it depends on conditions.

questions.question: At the December 2014 press conference, how did the Chair interpret the statement that the Committee can be patient?
questions.reference_answer: As meaning that the Committee is unlikely to begin the normalization process for at least the next couple of meetings, with no preset date and depending on the data.

questions.question: What did the Chair say about bitcoin at the December 2017 press conference?
questions.reference_answer: Yellen said bitcoin plays a very small role in the payment system, is not a stable store of value, is not legal tender and is a highly speculative asset, and that the Fed has no regulatory role beyond making sure supervised banks manage their interactions with it.

questions.question: How did the Chair describe the June 2022 75 basis point increase, and what did he say about the next meeting?
questions.reference_answer: Powell called it an unusually large increase and said he did not expect moves of this size to be common; either 50 or 75 basis points seemed most likely at the next meeting.

questions.question: At the June 2013 press conference, what path for asset purchases did the Chairman describe?
questions.reference_answer: If the data were consistent with the Committee's forecast, moderating purchases later in 2013, reducing them in measured steps through the first half of 2014 and ending them around midyear, when unemployment would likely be in the vicinity of 7 percent.

questions.question: What task forces did the Chair announce at the June 2026 press conference?
questions.reference_answer: Chairman Warsh announced five task forces: Fed communications, the balance sheet, the use of data sources, productivity and jobs, and inflation frameworks.

questions.question: At the June 2026 press conference, what did the Chair say about forward guidance and about his own economic projections?
questions.reference_answer: Warsh said forward guidance was absent from the statement because it was not well suited to the current conjuncture, and that he refrained from submitting his own projections to the SEP.

questions.question: According to the minutes of the January 2012 meeting, what longer-run inflation goal did the Committee adopt?
questions.reference_answer: Inflation at the rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures.

questions.question: Who abstained when the Committee reaffirmed its Statement on Longer-Run Goals in January 2013, and why?
questions.reference_answer: Mr. Tarullo, because he did not think the statement had advanced the cause of achieving or communicating greater consensus in the Committee's policy views.

questions.question: What did the Committee decide about principles for reducing the size of the balance sheet, according to the minutes of its January 2022 meeting?
questions.reference_answer: All participants supported the proposed principles, and the Committee voted unanimously to adopt the Principles for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet, while keeping flexibility to adjust details.

questions.question: What did the FOMC publish about policy normalization at its September 2014 meeting, according to the minutes?
questions.reference_answer: The Policy Normalization Principles and Plans, presented as prudent planning that did not imply normalization would begin soon; many of the principles adopted in June 2011 remained applicable.

questions.question: What options for the SOMA portfolio did the staff present at the September 2011 FOMC meeting?
questions.reference_answer: A reinvestment maturity extension program, a SOMA portfolio maturity extension program, and a large-scale asset purchase program.

questions.question: What views on a standing repo facility did participants express at the October 2019 FOMC meeting?
questions.reference_answer: Many saw little need for one once ample reserves were firmly established, while many also saw a role even with ample reserves; more work was needed on design choices such as pricing, eligible counterparties and collateral, and on risks such as moral hazard and stigma.

questions.question: According to the minutes of the June 2026 meeting, what did participants say about the postmeeting statement?
questions.reference_answer: A majority saw advantages in shortening it, and most preferred not to repeat the earlier language suggesting an easing bias; members agreed the statement would not repeat that language.

questions.question: According to the minutes of the June 2026 meeting, how did the market-implied path of the federal funds rate move over the intermeeting period, and why?
questions.reference_answer: It moved higher, along with nominal Treasury yields, as stronger-than-expected data reinforced expectations that economic activity would remain resilient.
